text:
Naveen P.: hi everyone, first week here! quick secrets question: trying to access a dev Vault secret for project 'atlas' but not sure whether I should request a role or a path grant. Also might need to decrypt a sample blob via KMS. whats the fastest route to get unblocked?

Tori H.: welcome Naveen! :wave: shortest path: open the onboarding portal and request specific Vault paths + tag kms-local-decrypt if you need KMS. we avoid granting broad roles.

Naveen P.: link to portal? and what fields are mandatory?

Tori H.: portal is https://internal.redwood.dev/onboard. mandatory: project slug, env, exact Vault paths (no values), reason, duration, and your github id. if you need KMS include the key name and whether it's for a human or service account. example to paste into the form:

Project: atlas
Env: dev
Vault paths: secret/projects/atlas/api_key, secret/projects/atlas/thirdparty/oauth
Reason: run local integration tests and reproduce bug #789
Duration: 7 days
GitHub: naveenp
KMS: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/dev/cryptoKeys/atlas-test (human decrypt)

Eli K.: small ops tip: attach the minimal IAM policy snippet in the portal ticket for KMS. that speeds up reviews. for human decrypts we often issue a session-limited grant that expires in 8 hours.

security-bot: Automated reminder: do not paste secret values or private keys into tickets. Use path names and key ids only. See https://internal.redwood.dev/security/vault-guides and https://internal.redwood.dev/security/kms-guidelines.

Naveen P.: if I need to run a local script that decrypts several blobs, is that allowed or do I need to run from the dev bastion?

Tori H.: depends on sensitivity. For test blobs in dev we usually allow local decrypt with session credentials and require you use the secrets-helper to inject into env vars (no files). For production keys we require bastion or ephemeral compute. Put 'local-decrypt' in the ticket and note where the script will run.

Eli K.: rotation note: if the work touches key rotation, include a rollback plan and the cadence wanted. Security will ask for a runbook for prod rotations. dev/test rotations are automated with a 30d TTL.

ops-bot: Automated: include policy example if requesting KMS decrypt. Minimal example at https://internal.redwood.dev/security/kms-guidelines#examples

Naveen P.: perfect, thanks all. I'll open the portal ticket now with the template and tag kms-local-decrypt. pinging @Tori H. if the approval needs a fast-track. :thumbsup:
